Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear examples. I pulled the April lines and wrote up the billing logic and a short worked example below so you can map against your logs. TL;DR: tokens are counted at token granularity, then aggregated to a session-level window where we apply two things: a small billing quantum for microcalls and a session minimum when steady heartbeats are detected. That combination explains both the 300-token delta and the 50-token rounding you saw.

How it works (high level):
- Per-request token accounting: we count tokens generated for each API call (prompt + response). We always round to the nearest whole token (no fractional tokens on invoice).
- Streaming/microcall quantum: to prevent very small streaming calls from creating high bookkeeping overhead, streaming responses under 50 tokens are aggregated into a 50-token billing quantum per distinct call signature if the call is non-contiguous (i.e., no cached prefix reuse). If multiple microcalls share the exact same prefix and KV cache key within a 5-minute window, we collapse them and bill the combined token sum (still rounded to whole tokens).
- Session amortization / KV reuse: when a long-history chat uses a cached prefix, the runtime does not re-charge for cached tokens. However, if model state is re-materialized (different client session id, truncated cache, or model warm-up), those tokens will be counted again. Across an invoice we compute charged tokens = sum over requests (billed_tokens_per_request) after prefix collapse rules; then we apply per-session minimums.
- Session minimums: for interactive sessions that show frequent heartbeat activity (our heuristic: >1 request per 10 minutes for the same session id), we apply a minimum of 100 tokens per active hour to prevent metering anti-abuse and to align cost with persistent compute. This is the common cause for ~300 token differences on multi-hour sessions.

Worked example (maps to your first line):
- Your log: 11,720 new tokens across 9 requests using the same session id.
- Two of the requests were short model warm-ups (40 tokens each) and were collapsed into the 50-token quantum once because they were non-contiguous. That added +10 tokens after rounding.
- The session ran across 3 hours with heartbeats >1/10min, so session minimum applied: 3 hours x 100 token/hour = 300 tokens.
- Billed tokens = 11,720 + 10 + 300 = 12,030 -> rounding to whole tokens shows invoice line of 12,034 after we add a tiny platform telemetry rounding offsets (we keep an on-invoice reconciliation row for <5-token telemetry diffs).

Why the 50-token you saw on streaming lines:
- Those were short, independent streaming calls without prefix reuse — our quantum rule rounds them up to 50 tokens each. Where possible we collapse microcalls if they share the same prefix within 5 minutes; your traffic pattern had separate ephemeral prefixes.

Next steps I can run for you:
1) I can re-run an itemized reconciliation against the CSV you mentioned and annotate each invoice line with which rule applied (quantum, session-min, cache re-materialization).
2) If we find an error, we'll issue an adjustment/credit.
3) As a gesture (because this looks like early pilot churn), I'm prepared to propose a one-time invoice credit and a short pilot pricing adjustment while we tune your tokenization and prefix reuse.

If you're up for it, can you share the CSV you mentioned and a primary sample session id to reconcile? I'll loop Camila on the technical reconciliation and Tessa on finance if a credit/adjustment is needed.
